chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Tatana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem narrated to us from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever says in every day of Sha'ban seventy times, 'I seek forgiveness of God and I ask Him for repentance,' God Almighty will record for him freedom from the Fire and a permit to cross the Bridge, and will let him enter the Eternal Residence.

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.شَعْبَان: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting a specific dhikr seventy times daily in the month of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this tradition highlights the spiritual significance of the month of Sha'ban as a period of preparation for Ramadan through consistent repentance. The promise of 'freedom from Hellfire' and 'entry into the Eternal Residence' underscores the Shia emphasis on the intercessory power of sincere *istighfar* (seeking forgiveness) in securing salvation and ease on the Day of Judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-212 Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Tatana - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt that he had heard Abal Hassan Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) say,

“God will record securityfrom the Fire and issue a permit to pass over the Bridge for whoever seeks God’s forgiveness by saying seventy times on each day of the (Arabic) month of Sha’ban, I ask God for forgiveness and to Him I repent. And God will let him enter the Eternal Residence.”
